skill.name: threejs-webgl
skill.description: Build interactive Three.js scenes with guidance on cameras, materials, lighting, model loading, animation, and performance. Includes a WebGL starter and scene generation tooling.
skill.summary: Create and optimize interactive Three.js scenes with reusable examples, reference guides, and a WebGL starter.
skill.author: freshtechbro

security_audit.summary: All 75 static findings are false positives: documented CDN imports, Markdown formatting, GLSL strings, and graphics terminology. The version-pinned CDN imports load rendering dependencies, with no evidence of data exfiltration. No evidence found of prompt injection or malicious intent in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: For hundreds/thousands of identical objects, use `InstancedMesh` (see pattern above).
Always call `.dispose()` on geometries, materials, textures, and renderers when no longer needed.
- `api_reference.md`: Quick API reference for core classes (Scene, Camera, Renderer, etc.)
- `setup_scene.py`: Generate boilerplate Three.js scene setup code
- `texture_optimizer.py`: Batch optimize textures for web (resize, compress)
- **Near plane**: As far as possible (avoid z-fighting)

content.value_statement: Building browser-based 3D scenes requires coordinating rendering, assets, interaction, and performance. This skill provides Three.js examples, reference guides, and a WebGL starter to support implementation.
actual_capabilities: Provides an animated WebGL starter with orbit controls, shadows, tone mapping, and window resize handling.
Includes a Python scene generator with configurable camera, background, lighting, and WebGL or WebGPU templates.
Explains material selection, PBR properties, texture color spaces, lighting, and shadow configuration.
Shows glTF loading, Draco loader configuration, and model animation patterns.
Demonstrates raycasting, GSAP animation, bloom post-processing, GLSL shaders, and render targets.
Provides performance guidance for instancing, resource reuse, level of detail, disposal, and mobile rendering.
limitations: The starter fetches Three.js 0.160.0 from jsDelivr and requires a local server or equivalent hosting.
WebGPU scaffolding is incomplete and needs rendering and compatibility checks before use.
The documented texture optimizer, model validator, and additional shader, environment, and decoder asset folders are not bundled.
React integration is delegated to another skill; examples require project integration and testing on target devices.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Product Viewer
use_cases.description: Adapt the WebGL starter to display a supplied product model with orbit controls, lighting, and selectable materials.

use_cases.title: Explore Materials and Shaders
use_cases.description: Compare PBR settings and adapt GLSL examples for interactive visual experiments.

use_cases.title: Improve Mobile Rendering
use_cases.description: Use the optimization checklist to investigate draw calls, texture memory, shadow cost, and repeated object rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic Three.js WebGL scene with a rotating cube, orbit controls, lighting, and resize handling. Explain the required dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Load a Product Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the starter to load my supplied glTF product model. Add selectable material colors, shadows, and loading errors without assuming decoder assets are bundled.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my supplied Three.js scene and profiling results for mobile performance. Prioritize instancing, texture sizes, pixel ratio, shadows, and disposal with measurable checks.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a Shader Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate an animated GLSL material and render target into my supplied WebGL scene. Define uniform updates, cleanup, fallback behavior, and device verification.

output_examples.input: Create a simple interactive Three.js demo.
output: Scene structure with a perspective camera, WebGL renderer, and orbit controls.
Animated cube, sphere, and torus with PBR materials and shadow lighting.
Resize handling and a checklist for checking the demo in a browser.

output_examples.input: My mobile scene slows down when hundreds of objects appear.
output: A prioritized review of draw calls, geometry duplication, texture resolution, and shadow settings.
An instancing proposal for repeated meshes, with shared materials and a lower pixel ratio.
Before-and-after measurements for frame time, draw calls, and resource counts.

output_examples.input: Plan a viewer for my glTF product model.
output: A model loading plan with progress, error handling, and camera framing.
Material and lighting choices for the supplied product.
Separate requirements for external decoder assets, animation updates, and resource cleanup.

best_practices: Match examples and addon imports to the installed Three.js version, and provide required model, texture, and decoder assets explicitly.
Profile on target devices before changing geometry, texture resolution, shadow maps, or post-processing.
Reuse geometry and materials, update camera dimensions on resize, and dispose unused rendering resources.
anti_patterns: Treating generated WebGPU scaffolding as a complete application without verifying its render loop.
Assuming every tool or asset mentioned in the documentation is included in the package.
Allocating geometry every frame or enabling expensive shadows and effects without profiling.

faq.question: What does this skill include?
faq.answer: It includes Three.js guidance, API and material references, an optimization checklist, a scene generator, and an animated WebGL starter.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The underlying examples use JavaScript and Python.

faq.question: Does the starter work without internet access?
faq.answer: Not as bundled. It loads version-pinned Three.js modules from jsDelivr; use locally hosted dependencies for offline operation.

faq.question: Is WebGPU support ready to use?
faq.answer: The skill provides WebGPU guidance and scaffolding. The generated animation function lacks a render call, so complete and verify it before use.

faq.question: Are model validation and texture optimization tools included?
faq.answer: No. The documentation mentions these tools, but only the scene generator is present in the supplied scripts.

faq.question: Does this skill include a React implementation?
faq.answer: No. It points to a separate React Three Fiber skill; its bundled starter uses plain JavaScript.
